subject: Normalization playbook: cross-team slotting & edge cases
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@people-partners.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Normalization playbook: cross-team slotting & edge cases

Team —

As we finalize Q1 calibration, I want to surface a short playbook for how we normalize slotting decisions across eng teams. The problem: several teams have a cluster of borderline ratings this cycle (mostly 3 vs 4) and the current guidance still leaves room for manager-level inflation.

Please review the attached roster and the slotting examples PDF before our sync. Prework asks:
- Flag any direct reports you believe should move between bands but need cross-team alignment (add a short rationale in the roster)
- Identify any role-skewed comparisons (IC vs IC+mentor, architect vs IC)
- Note candidate edge cases in the "edge-case" column (e.g., long-term contractor converted mid-cycle, extended leave)

Meeting: Tue Feb 22, 1:00–2:00 PT (calendar invite attached). Opening document is here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1XNote-normalization-playbook

Attachments: calibration-roster-2027-Q1.xlsx, slotting-guidelines-examples.pdf

Goal: produce a one-pager with clear decision rules and a list of final slot changes we can hand to HR for sign-off.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Director, Engineering 
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@people-partners.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Normalization playbook: cross-team slotting & edge cases

Neha — thanks for pulling this together. I uploaded three borderline cases to the roster (rows 12–14) and attached a short doc with role context I think will help the panel.

Quick note on one case: Raj P. has heavy influence duties (mentorship + cross-team fixes) but fewer measurable launches; I put a proposed compromise (3.5 slot / calibration note) in the notes column.

Attachment: edge-case-notes-lb.docx

— Lauren
Senior Engineering Manager

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena@people-partners.com>
Date: 2027-02-20T13:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Normalization playbook: cross-team slotting & edge cases

Thanks — I reviewed the roster. Two concerns from infra:

1) Manager-level skew: team beta had three 4s where calibration against other infra squads suggests a slight upward compression. We should apply a normalization factor when comparing across squads with different throughput metrics.
2) Converted contractor: row 9 (A. Gomez) worked 9 months as contractor; if we treat the full-year performance, it inflates the comparison for PR purposes. I recommend we weight converted contractors at 0.8 for slotting decisions and call that out in the one-pager.

Happy to surface empirical examples in the meeting.

— Marcus
Engineering Manager, Infra

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@people-partners.com>
Date: 2027-02-21T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Normalization playbook: cross-team slotting & edge cases

Neha / all —

Strong framing. A few process asks from leadership:
- We need a hard decision rule for converted roles and extended leaves (Marcus’ 0.8 suggestion is a fine starting point if it helps prevent inconsistent outcomes).
- Anything that changes a compensation band requires a written calibration rationale (one paragraph) and a senior manager sign-off before HR executes.
- For transparency, we'll publish the one-pager plus an anonymized appendix showing distribution shifts by team.

Also: can Marissa take point on consolidating notes into the one-pager after the session? Marissa, please confirm.

Vivek
VP, Engineering Operations

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena@people-partners.com>, Joe Sloper <joe.sloper@acme-dev.com>
Date: 2027-02-21T11:50:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Normalization playbook: cross-team slotting & edge cases

Marissa — thank you for taking this. I've added an updated roster v1.2 with a "rationale" column and a short template for the paragraph we need for any band changes (see attachment).

Attaching: calibration-roster-2027-Q1.xlsx (v1.2)

One logistical ask: if we end up applying a normalization factor we should call out the multiplier explicitly in the one-pager and list impacted headcount so compensation can stage approvals.

Neha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Normalization playbook: cross-team slotting & edge cases
